title: Text another user wrote runs as script in a customer's page

source.kind: a CVE, the advisory of the app that had it (Open WebUI, a SvelteKit app); security guidance; W3C specification
source.date: CVE-2025-46719 published by NVD 2025-05-05, reviewed by GitHub 2026-07-07, read 2026-10-15; S21, S27 2026-09-10, as read for the census
source.says: Open WebUI before 0.6.6 (a SvelteKit app: `@sveltejs/kit` in its package.json, read 2026-10-15) rendered an HTML token of a chat message with `{@html `${token.text}`}` (MarkdownTokens.svelte): a stored XSS, rated high, which the advisory takes to account takeover; it calls `{@html}` "a dangerous Svelte functionality". the census's reading: output contexts need different treatment, and safe text sinks, validated URLs and audited HTML sanitization are not interchangeable (S21); Trusted Types constrains values entering injection sinks through explicit policies (S27)

claim: charter §8.2 (escaping is the default); `html.raw_html` performs `unsafe.raw_html`, and reaching it needs an audited capability with a justification (PW5010)

repro.how: T09's store notice, which staff post, rendered with Svelte's `{@html}` so that its formatting shows; the repair renders it as text, `{data.notice}`, which Svelte escapes

pleris.faithful: The same notice, on the same store (T09's setup), rendered through `html.raw_html`: refused, naming the capability and the escaped alternative. Its neighbour is T09's `{notice}`, escaped by default.
